condition.narrative: Delivery of a completed Disbursement Request, together with the periodic reports required under Section 5.1 of this Agreement, in each case in form and substance satisfactory to MCC, covering the related Disbursement Period.

Each of the Government�s representations and warranties set forth in Section 4.1 of this Agreement are true and correct on and as of the date on which the Disbursement Request is submitted and as though made on and as of such date.

Evidence of Tax Exemption Mechanism: MCC is satisfied that the Government has entered into a tax exemption agreement or such other mechanism acceptable to MCC to establish or give effect to Section 4.2(j), and such mechanisms are in full force and effect.

Fiscal Agent Services: Designation of an entity or individual to provide fiscal agent services, as approved by MCC, until such time as the Government provides to MCC a true and complete copy of the Fiscal Agent Agreement, duly executed and in full force and effect, and the Fiscal Agent engaged thereby is mobilized.
If requested by MCC, delivery of a certificate from the Procurement Agent in form and substance satisfactory to MCC.
If requested by MCC, delivery of a certificate from the Fiscal Agent in form and substance satisfactory to MCC.
If requested by MCC, delivery of a certificate from the Government in form and substance satisfactory to MCC.
If requested by MCC, delivery of a certificate from the Permitted Designee in form and substance satisfactory to MCC.

Initial Disbursements to a Permitted Account: Prior to an initial Disbursement of any Grant funding to a Permitted Account, a true and complete copy of each Bank Agreement, duly executed and in full force and effect as of the date of the related Disbursement Request.
Interim Fiscal Accountability Plan: Adoption of an Interim Fiscal Accountability Plan acceptable to MCC.

No material breach of any responsibility, covenant or obligation under this Agreement or any other related agreement (including the Bank Agreement, the Fiscal Agent Agreement, the Procurement Agent Agreement and any Government Service Provider Contract) by any Permitted Designee has occurred and is continuing on and as of the date of the Disbursement Request.

Prior to any disbursement of the Grant for the MCC-Contracted Activities that would be subject to taxation by the Government but for this Section 3.1(b), the Government shall have entered into a tax exemption agreement or have implemented such other mechanism acceptable to MCC to establish or give effect to Section 4.2(j), and such mechanism shall be in full force and effect.

Procurement Agent Services: Designation of an entity or individual to provide procurement agent services, as approved by MCC, until such time as the Government provides to MCC a true and complete copy of the Procurement Agent Agreement, duly executed and in full force and effect, and the Procurement Agent engaged thereby is mobilized.
Satisfaction of each of the conditions set forth in Section 3.4.

condition.narrative: The Cote d'Ivoire Regional Compact may be suspended or terminated, among other conditions, if Cote d'Ivoire (i) fails to comply with its commitments under the agreements entered into with MCC in relation to the program, (ii) engages in a pattern of actions inconsistent with the criteria used by MCC to determine eligibility for the program, or (iii) engages in activities contrary to the national security interests of the United States. Disbursements of funding under a Compact Program are subject to specific conditions set forth in the Compact Program agreement for the individual projects funded thereby, as well as general conditions, such as the delivery of implementation, fiscal accountability, and monitoring and evaluation plans.

title.narrative: Cote d'Ivoire-Compact

description.narrative:
The MCC Board of Directors approved a $524.7 million compact for Cote d'Ivoire at its quarterly board meeting in September 2017. The Government of Cote d'Ivoire is expected to contribute an additional $22 million to support the compact. The program will support the country's drive to diversify its economy through investments in the education and transportation sectors. The Projects respond to constraints to economic growth in Cote d'Ivoire, and the Government's national priorities by seeking to address education and the competitiveness of Abidjan as the country's economic growth hub by improving the mobility of goods and people.
On August 5, 2025, the Millennium Challenge Corporation and the Government of Cote d'Ivoire marked the closeout of the catalytic compact that improved critical transport infrastructure and strengthened public education and workforce development, all to help unlock the full potential of the Ivorian workforce and economy.

(xiii) MCA-C�te d�Ivoire has complied in all material respects with its obligations set forth in Section 2.1(d) with respect to the establishment of a BCS and its obligations set forth in Section 2.3 with respect to the establishment of an M&E Plan.
Each of the Key Staff has been selected and engaged by MCA-C�te d�Ivoire and approved by MCC.

Prior to any Disbursement of Program Funding after the commencement of year five (5) of the Compact Term, the Government must have submitted to MCC an initial draft Compact Closure Plan in accordance with the MCC Program Closure Guidelines.

Prior to entry into force of the Compact, MCA-C�te d�Ivoire must have developed and adopted an environmental and social management system (�ESMS�), including a stakeholder engagement plan, in accordance with MCC�s Environmental Guidelines as evidenced by (a) a resolution of the MCA-C�te d�Ivoire Board of Directors adopting the ESMS; (b) the corresponding staffing plan, training plan and budget for implementing the ESMS; and (c) public disclosure of the ESMS and stakeholder engagement plan on the MCA-C�te d�Ivoire�s website. In addition, MCA-C�te d�Ivoire agrees to maintain and implement the ESMS throughout the life of the Compact and through up to 90 days of the closure period including retaining sufficient technical resources and budget to operate the ESMS in form and substance satisfactory to MCC.

Prior to entry into force of the Compact, MCA-C�te d�Ivoire must procure the services of the environmental and social oversight consultant (�ESOC�) with adequate technical capacity to ensure the implementation of all Compact activities in accordance with MCC�s Environmental Guidelines, including the IFC Performance Standards. MCA-C�te d�Ivoire must maintain the ESOC in form and substance satisfactory to MCC through the Compact Term and up to 90 days of the Compact closure period.

Prior to the Disbursement of Program Funding for payment under a particular works or construction contract for a given Project or Activity, MCA-C�te d�Ivoire must have submitted to MCC evidence that MCA-C�te d�Ivoire or an appropriate Government entity has developed and adopted, or validated, as the case may be, (i) an environmental and social impact assessment (�ESIA�) with underlying environmental and social management plan (�ESMP�), (ii) a resettlement action plan (�RAP�), and (iii) a restoration of livelihood plan (as appropriate), acceptable to MCC, with respect to such Project or Activity. Contractor access to the construction site will not be granted until project affected persons have been compensated and relocated (as appropriate), and the site has been secured.
Prior to the second Disbursement of Program Funding, MCA-C�te d�Ivoire must have developed and approved a comprehensive Social and Gender Integration Plan.
The Government must have adopted any documents necessary to create MCA-C�te d�Ivoire and ensure its valid operation, including, but not limited to, any required laws, decrees or regulations.

title.narrative: EDUCATION AND TRAINING FOR EMPLOYABILITY PROJECT

description.narrative: Cote d'Ivoire - EDUCATION AND TRAINING FOR EMPLOYABILITY PROJECT: The Skills for Employability and Productivity Project will increase access to secondary education and teacher training, and support the construction of up to 84 new secondary schools. Through a public-private partnership, a new technical vocational education and training (TVET) model will advance development of in-demand skills. It will also help the government mitigate gender disparities, improving outcomes for girls in the education system.

title.narrative: Cote d'Ivoire Compact Key Performance Indicators

condition.narrative: Further details on conditions precedent affecting this activity can be found in the top-level parent activities.

Prior to Disbursement for construction of secondary schools under the Equitable Access Sub-Activity in the second tranche in Gb�k�, the Government must have (a) adopted the new Gender Policy under the Gender Policy Sub-Activity, (b) established a Gender Unit with an adopted staffing model, (c) incorporated the Gender Unit into the Ministry of National Education organizational chart, (d) established a budget line item in the Ministry of National Education�s budget to support the Gender Unit�s activities, and (e) allocated the funding necessary for the operationalization, functioning and sustainability of the Gender Unit for that current fiscal year.

Prior to the Disbursement of Program Funding for the construction of secondary schools under the Equitable Access Sub-Activity after 18 months after entry into force of the Compact, the Ministry of National Education must have provisionally deployed inspecteurs to Gb�k� and San Pedro and provided those inspecteurs with adequate operational budgets to conduct supportive supervision of teachers in those regions, which budget should cover vehicle operations and maintenance.

Prior to the Disbursement of Program Funding for the construction of secondary schools under the Equitable Access Sub-Activity after 24 months after entry into force of the Compact, the Parties agree to perform an interim performance review of progress on school construction during the Compact, and consider whether any modifications or other changes to the Activity are necessary.

title.narrative: Employed graduates of MCC-supported education activities

description.narrative: Cumulative Outcome of According to the TVET Activity work plans and as reflected in Annex II of the M&E Plan, reporting on this indicator was expected to start during year 5 of the compact, following completion of the construction of the TVET centers. The construction of the TVET centers did not begin until 2024 and will not be completed until after the end of the compact, with the first cohorts of students expected to enroll in 2026. Thus, when taking into account the definition of this indicator, the earliest that data could reasonably be expected would be 2027. This indicator will be reported on as part of the independent evaluation of the TVET Activity, with the final evaluation report expected in 2030.

title.narrative: Graduates from MCC-supported education activities

description.narrative: Cumulative Outcome of According to the TVET Activity work plans and as reflected in Annex II of the M&E Plan, reporting on this indicator was expected to start during year 5 of the compact, following completion of the construction of the TVET centers. The construction of the TVET centers did not begin until 2024 and will not be completed until after the end of the compact, with the first cohorts of students expected to enroll in 2026. In order to be counted under this indicator, an individual must complete all relevant coursework, successfully complete the certification exam, and receive a graduation certificate. Thus, the earliest that data could reasonably be expected would be late 2026 or early 2027. This indicator will be reported on as part of the independent evaluation of the TVET Activity, with the final evaluation report expected in 2030.

title.narrative: Gross enrollment rate for school-aged children in the catchment areas of Compact-supported lower-secondary schools

description.narrative: Level Outcome of This indicator is defined as the proportion of children enrolled in Compact-supported lower-secondary schools over the population of children of the official age (12-15 years) to be enrolled in lower-secondary school. For the numerator, the first set of 13 lower-secondary schools (CDPs) were completed in the fall of 2024 and enrolled 873 students in the first year of lower secondary school (6th). However, the denominator for this indicator - population of children of the official age to be enrolled in lower-secondary school - was not available for the 2024-2025 school year and therefore this indicator could not be calculated. That being said, during the previous school year 2023-2024, 44,330 students were enrolled in the last year of primary school (CM2) in all the villages of the Compact catchment areas. Using this figure, the gross enrollment rate can be estimated at around 2% for the 2024-2025 school year.

title.narrative: Gross intake ratio for students in the last year of Compact-supported lower-secondary schools

description.narrative: Level Outcome of Due to delays in implementation of the Secondary Education Activity, the first lower-secondary schools were not completed until the fall of 2024. These schools only enrolled students for the first two years of lower secondary school, except for the lower-secondary school of Ti�pl� (Gb�k�) which enrolled 8 students for the last year of lower secondary school. Given the fact that three of the four schools open for the 2024/2025 school year intentionally did not enroll students for the last year of lower-secondary, this indicator was not calculated. Data for the 2025/2026 school year was not yet available at Compact closeout and therefore has not been reported. As a result, there will be no data reported for this indicator by the end of the Compact.

title.narrative: Students benefitting from improved teacher training

description.narrative: Level Outcome of According to Annex II of the Monitoring and Evaluation Plan, this indicator was to be reported for the first time in year 6 (July 24 to August 25) of the Compact. The student teachers trained on the new curriculum completed their training in July 2024. To collect this indicator, it is necessary to have the distribution of 966 bivalent teachers throughout the country and then determine the number of students taught by each of them in their schools of assignment. Due to the logistical difficulties related to the data collection process throughout the country, the time remaining before the Compact closing and the fact that the Boussole platform to track teachers is not yet used at the national level, this indicator could not be calculated. Therefore, no data will be reported for this indicator by the end of the Compact.

title.narrative: Students participating in MCC-supported education activities

description.narrative: Cumulative Outcome of According to the TVET Activity work plans and as reflected in Annex II of the M&E Plan, reporting on this indicator was expected to start during year 5 of the compact, following completion of the construction of the TVET centers. The construction of the TVET centers did not begin until 2024 and will not be completed until after the end of the compact, with the first cohorts of students expected to enroll in 2026. This indicator will be reported on as part of the independent evaluation of the TVET Activity, with the final evaluation report expected in 2030.

title.narrative: TVET accreditation obtained for Compact-supported TVET centers

description.narrative: Cumulative Outcome of According to the TVET Activity work plans and as reflected in Annex II of the M&E Plan, reporting on this indicator was expected to start during year 5 of the compact, following completion of the construction of the TVET centers. The construction of the TVET centers did not begin until 2024 and will not be completed until after the end of the compact, with the first cohorts of students expected to enroll in 2026. The TVET centers must be fully operational with students enrolled in order to begin the accreditation process. Thus, as a result of the delays in implementation of the TVET Activity, the compact-supported TVET centers will not obtain accreditation prior to the end of the compact. This indicator will be reported on as part of the independent evaluation of the TVET Activity, with the final evaluation report expected in 2030.

title.narrative: Catchment areas where priority action items have been implemented

description.narrative: Cumulative Output of The priority actions were implemented in two phases: Phase 1 took into account the priority actions carried out without the lower secondary schools supported by the Compact being functional and includes missions 2A, 5A and 8A. Phase 2 concerned priority actions requiring a functional lower secondary schools and includes missions 3A, 4A, 6A and 7A. The various missions of Phase 1 carried out can be summarized as: (i) Sensitization of customary and religious authorities, local authorities and parents of students on sex-based equality and equity in education, as well as the various national and international legal instruments and constraints related to girls' education (in particular GBV, pregnancies during school, FGM) through the production and broadcasting of radio programs, the organization of discussion forums, the production and distribution of printed matter and films, etc.; (ii) The establishment and/or strengthening of the involvement of women's associations (CMEF, women's groups) in school life in areas with high drop-outs of girls and low transition to secondary education and (iii) The increase in learners' participation in formal secondary education. Those of Phase 2 can be summarized as: (i) Training of teachers, secondary school administrative and supervisory staff, GSCs and students on GBV, in-school pregnancies, sexual harassment, student participation in schools, the various child protection instruments, the child-friendly school and girl-friendly approach (EAEAF) and strategies for the reintegration of young mothers; (ii) The establishment of mechanisms for the collection, prevention and care of GBV at the regional, departmental, sub-prefectural and CoPs levels, in close collaboration with the DRENAs and the Regional Directorates for Women, Family and Children; (iii) Raising awareness among girls to take an interest in science, technology, engineering and mathematics and (iv) setting up and supporting the operation of a mentoring system for girls in science and mathematics. As of June 30, 2025, here are the results for each phase: - Phase 1: Of the 40 Compact catchment areas (12 in San Pedro and 28 in Gb�k�), 12 catchment areas in the San Pedro region (Adjam�n�, Oueoulo, Man�, Youwasso, Blahou, Fah�, Grobonou Dan, Gnity, Hannie, Para, Mahino 1 and Gbapet) and 18 in the Gb�k� region (Bendekouassikro, Ti�pl�, Mamini, Krofouinssou, Sins�kro, Akadiafoue, Belakro, Golibl�nou, Kanangopkli, Andofouebonou, Lolobo, Ahougnanfoutou, Adjougouansou, N'Dakro, Sran-Belakro, Klemeklo, Kondoukro and Koblekro) have fully benefited from all the priority actions planned. The remaining 10 catchment areas are new. The various missions were not planned to be carried out in these new catchment areas. Only three tasks of mission 2A were carried out by AETS during Q24; the other tasks could not be carried out due to the short time remaining. The Phase 1 action items were also implemented in six catchment areas that were not funded by the Compact. However, the full set of action items were not completed in any of these areas so therefore are not counted here. - Phase 2: Of the 40 Compact catchment areas (12 in San Pedro and 28 in Gb�k�), 5 catchment areas in the San Pedro region (Adjam�n�, Man�, Youwasso, Blahou and Fah�) and 8 in Gb�k� (Ti�pl�, Mamini, Krofouinssou, Sinz�kro, Golibl�nou, Andofouebonou, Adjougouansou and N'Dakro) have fully benefited from all the priority actions planned. As the remaining 27 catchment areas did not open in time, the tasks could not be carried out.

title.narrative: Classrooms constructed and ready for use

description.narrative: Cumulative Output of Initially, the Compact planned for the construction of 752 classrooms. This target was not reached due to an increase in school construction costs and delays related, among other reasons, to the COVID-19 pandemic. In August 2024, a Compact modification was approved that finalized the scope of lower-secondary school construction at 496 classrooms within 40 schools. The M&E Plan states that this indicator will count classrooms when schools are completely equipped and prepared for the first day of classes. The required source documents include construction completion certificates, equipment delivery receipts, and utility connection certificates. By the end of the compact, source documents were signed and available for 36 of the 40 schools. At Compact End Date (CED), however, for several of the schools, the construction works were not substantially completed, and staff furniture and student desks were still being assembled. Thus, 440 is likely an overestimate of the number of classrooms ready for the first day of classes by CED, as per the definition set forth in the M&E Plan.

title.narrative: Compact-supported Integrated Educational Management Information System improvements deployed

description.narrative: Date Output of A workshop to validate the deployment of the EMIS no longer took place, but a gradual deployment of the EMIS was carried out and allowed the tools to be tested in real conditions before any enlargement (see Section 4.6, Page 22, C2D Final Report). Subsequently, training sessions were organised to enable the various profiles of actors in the education sector to master the modules of the EMIS, to ensure their functional use on a daily basis and to prepare the regional and technical relays with a view to scaling up (see Section 4.7, Page 24, C2D Final Report). The sessions were effectively launched in the regions of Bouak� and San-Pedro on May 12, 2025 and the last training session was held from July 21-25, 2025 in Abidjan. Based on the final report by C2D, the EMIS was not completed during the Compact. 5 main modules and 3 additional components were envisioned. However, as of the end of the Compact, "the progress of the functional components remains mixed: some blocks, such as the portal or the GES and RAD modules, are considered operational, while others, notably the GRH and GEC modules and the SIGFLUX engine, remain partially delivered or unstable."

title.narrative: DEEG Unit budget received

description.narrative: Level Output of For reasons of understanding the definition of the indicator, work was done with the Department of Budget which shared with MCA a document giving some explanations on the interpretation of variables in the budget file used to inform the indicator. CP Actuel is the budget to date. It shall take into account, where appropriate, all the changes resulting from the various budgetary acts which have been made to the initial budget. Budget received by the DEEG from the GoCI during the fiscal year 2024 (January 2024 to December 2024) is 25,000,000 FCFA francs against 20,894,754 FCFA, representing an annual increase of 19,64%. The data was submitted via a HACR for Q22.

title.narrative: Educational facilities constructed or rehabilitated

description.narrative: Cumulative Output of The M&E Plan states that this indicator will count teacher training campuses when they are completely equipped and prepared for the first day of classes. The required source documents include construction completion certificates, receipt of equipment delivery, and certification for connection of all utilities. By the end of the compact, construction completion certificates and equipment delivery receipts were shared for both campuses. Unique utility connection certificates were not shared, but the reception report validated that utilities were connected. At Compact End Date, however, for the San Pedro campus, the construction works were not substantially completed, and staff furniture and student desks were not completely installed. Thus, 2 is likely an overestimate of the number of teacher training campuses ready for the first day of classes by compact end date, as per the definition set forth in the M&E Plan.

title.narrative: Educational facilities constructed or rehabilitated

description.narrative: Cumulative Output of According to the TVET Activity work plans and Annex II of the M&E Plan, reporting on this indicator was expected to start during year 5 of the compact, following completion of the construction of the TVET centers. In order to be considered fully constructed and ready to receive students, a TVET center must not only have completed major works but also be equipped, have all utilities connected, and comply with relevant MCC and national policies regarding safety and security. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic combined with delays in implementation of the TVET Activity (delays and challenges with the process to select and sign agreements with the private sector consortia, delays in procuring construction works, etc.), the construction of the TVET centers did not begin until 2024 and will not be completed until after the end of the compact, with the first cohorts of students expected to enroll in 2026. This indicator will be reported on as part of the independent evaluation of the TVET Activity, with the final evaluation report expected in 2030.

title.narrative: Lower-secondary schools substantially completed

description.narrative: Cumulative Output of Initially, the Compact planned for at least 74 lower-secondary schools to be substantially completed. The target of 74 lower-secondary schools was not reached due to an increase in school construction costs and delays related, among other reasons, to the COVID-19 pandemic. In August 2024, a Compact modification was approved that finalized the scope of lower-secondary school construction at 40 schools. The M&E Plan states that this indicator will count schools when they are "sufficiently completed in accordance with the construction contract documents, so that classrooms and other facilities can be used for the intended purpose." The required source document is the construction completion certificate. By the end of the compact, source documents were signed and available for 36 of the 40 schools. At Compact End Date (CED), however, for several of the schools, the construction works were not substantially completed. Thus, 36 is likely an overestimate of the number of educational facilities ready for the first day of classes by CED, as per the definition set forth in the M&E Plan.

title.narrative: National assessment framework for lower-secondary schools developed

description.narrative:
Date Output of This indicator is considered complete and is not expected to be updated further.
The National Assessment Framework have been validated in August 2023 by MENA. After that, it took time to finalize the document (formatting, correction of mistakes, editing, etc.) but the final version of the document was released in June 2024. The report did not provide a specific date of validation, we considered the last day of the month as the date of validation
The National Assessment Framework lays the foundations of the assessment system in C�te d'Ivoire and takes into account classroom assessments, standardized national examinations, national and international assessments of learning outcomes, as well as learning assessments in literacy and non-formal education to measure and improve student and learner outcomes.

title.narrative: People trained in data interpretation and decision making

description.narrative: Cumulative Output of The EMIS design originally anticipated a multi-tiered training program, with different trainings for each of the modules. However, given delays in EMIS implementation, the trainings were combined and multiple modules were covered in the same training sessions. Most training sessions, therefore, included some discussion of data interpetation and decision making. To avoid counting the same training sessions twice, this indicator counts participants that participated in a training with Ministry of Education members on high-level data interpretation and decision making from 22-23 July.

However, given delays in EMIS implementation, the trainings were combined and multiple modules were covered in the same training sessions. Most training sessions, therefore, included some discussion of data interpetation and decision making. To avoid counting the same training sessions twice, this indicator counts participants that participated in general EMIS training sessions held in 2025 in: Bouake from 12-19 May, San Pedro from 22-27 May, and Abidjan from 23-June to 1-July, as well as participants of a training session on the detailed mechanics of the EMIS from 21-25 July. One additional training was held for Ministry of Education staff on high-level data interpretation and decision making from 22-23 July. The participants of this final training are counted for the "People trained in data interpretation and decision making" indicator below.

title.narrative: Tracer studies conducted in Compact-supported TVET centers

description.narrative: Cumulative Output of According to the TVET Activity work plans and as reflected in Annex II of the M&E Plan, reporting on this indicator was expected to start during year 5 of the compact, following completion of the construction of the TVET centers. The construction of the TVET centers did not begin until 2024 and will not be completed until after the end of the compact, with the first cohorts of students expected to enroll in 2026. Thus, when taking into account the definition of this indicator, the earliest that data could reasonably be expected would be 2027. As such, the end of compact target will not be met. This indicator will be reported on as part of the independent evaluation of the TVET Activity, with the final evaluation report expected in 2030.

title.narrative: Tracer studies system developed

description.narrative: Date Output of According to the TVET Activity work plans and as reflected in Annex II of the M&E Plan, the tracer studies system was expected to be developed by year 4 of Compact. The detailed functional architecture of the tracer system was approved in December 2022. The tracer system was subsequently tested in May 2024 in 3 non-project TVET centers located in Abidjan, Bouak� and San Pedro. The tracer system has also been rolled out and socialized with key stakeholders.However, the METFPA did not published the official document ("circulaire d'approbation") approving the tracer studies system until after the end of the compact.

title.narrative: TVET accreditation system developed

description.narrative: Date Output of According to the TVET Activity work plans and as reflected in Annex II of the M&E Plan, the development of the TVET accreditation system was expected to be completed in Year 4 of the compact. The accreditation system for TVET centers has been developed by SOFRECO in collaboration with the training supervisory unit of the TVET Ministry (METFPA) since July 2024. However, the METFPA did not published the official document ("circulaire d'approbation") approving the TVET accreditation system until after the end of the compact.

title.narrative: Potential villages selected

description.narrative: Cumulative Process of This indicator is considered complete and is not expected to be updated further. Community mobilization activities resulted in the selection of 73 villages in which CDPs could be built. However, the MCA had to suspend the identification of villages that could potentially host CDPs. Indeed, due to budgetary constraints, the Compact no longer had the resources to build 74 CDPs as initially planned. As a result, it was no longer relevant to continue the selection of villages in which the CDPs were likely to be built.

title.narrative: School sites selected

description.narrative: Cumulative Process of This indicator is considered complete and is not expected to be updated further. Initially, the compact planned to select 74 sites for the construction of at least 74 CDPs. Community mobilization activities resulted in the selection of 58 CDP construction sites (78%). The target of 74 sites was not reached due to budgetary constraints. Indeed, the initial budget planned for the construction of the CDPs were insufficient to cover the construction costs proposed by the selected firms. As a result, MCA had to stop site selection activities as the available resources did not allow for the construction of CDPs on all identified sites.

title.narrative: Value disbursed of educational facility construction, rehabilitation, and equipping contracts

description.narrative: Cumulative Process of Disbursements were made to 2 constructions firms and 5 equipment firm during the period of Q22-Q25. The discussion on 02/05/2024 between the M&E and Finance teams clarified the issue of exchange rates used in SAP. The system uses the exchange rate on the day of payment and automatically calculates gains or losses due to the variation of the exchange rate. The average exchange rate calculated at the beginning of each period is only used for the revaluation of contracts denominated in XOF but not for payments.

title.narrative: Value disbursed of educational facility construction, rehabilitation, and equipping contracts

description.narrative: Cumulative Process of Disbursements were made to 15 constructions firms , 5 service firm and 5 equipment firms during the period of Q23, Q24 and Q25. The discussion on 02/05/2024 between the M&E and Finance teams clarified the issue of exchange rates used in SAP. The system uses the exchange rate on the day of payment and automatically calculates gains or losses due to the variation of the exchange rate. The average exchange rate calculated at the begining of each period is only used for the revaluation of contracts denominated in XOF but not for payments. The unspecified amount refers to services delivered (books supplies) and communication services (school marking) for the 2 regions.

The termination of MYKA was not taken into account in the values of the contracts signed, as the necessary information was not provided by the project team.

title.narrative: TVET National Framework Activity

description.narrative: Cote d'Ivoire - EDUCATION AND TRAINING FOR EMPLOYABILITY PROJECT - TVET National Framework Activity: The TVET Activity complements the Secondary Education Activity through a new TVET model that provides training to students in the skills and knowledge in-demand by the private sector. This new TVET model will be implemented through new and sustainable training centers developed and managed through a public-private partnership with industries in Cote d'Ivoire. This new model will be implemented with a goal of catalyzing a shift within the training system towards better identifying and meeting the training needs of the private sector. The TVET Activity is made up of two sub-activities designed to implement and support this new TVET model: A New Model for Private Sector-Led TVET Sub-Activity - The New Model for Private Sector-Led TVET Sub-Activity will introduce and test a new model of "Partnerships for Skills Development" ("Partenariat pour le D�veloppement des Comp�tences" or "PDC") to provide training through direct partnerships with the private sector; TVET Quality Management and Accountability Sub-Activity - This sub-activity will create primary tools for quality management and accountability to create the enabling environment for a long-term reorientation of the TVET system towards results-based management.

title.narrative: Secondary Education Activity

description.narrative: Cote d'Ivoire - EDUCATION AND TRAINING FOR EMPLOYABILITY PROJECT - Secondary Education Activity: The Activity aims to increase access to lower secondary education in two regions of Cote d'Ivoire and improve the access to, and quality of, secondary education and the governance of the sector. The Activity will be pursued through four sub-activities that will invest in new education infrastructure, expand and improve teacher training, reduce gender disparities in educational outcomes, and enhance the Government's information management system and use of such system for decision-making in the national education sector.

condition.narrative: Further details on conditions precedent affecting this activity can be found in the top-level parent activities.

Prior to Disbursement of Program Funding for the Secondary Education Activity, the Government must have established an inter-ministerial teacher training committee with representatives from Ministry of Higher Education (including ENS), Ministry of National Eduction, Ministry of Economy and Finances, Ministry of Budget, and Ministry of Public Service, and the committee will have held its first meeting.

Prior to the Disbursement of Program Funding for equipment and materials for the ENS Abidjan campus or its practicum school, the ENS must adopt the new teacher training curriculum under the Teacher Training Sub-Activity.

Prior to the Disbursement of Program Funding for the Integrated EMIS, an inter-departmental committee will have been established within the Ministry of National Education to coordinate the Management Systems Sub-Activity and facilitate change management during the transition to the Integrated EMIS

usg:usg-activity.usg:purpose-statement: Cote d'Ivoire - EDUCATION AND TRAINING FOR EMPLOYABILITY PROJECT - Secondary Education Activity: The Activity aims to increase access to lower secondary education in two regions of Cote d'Ivoire and improve the access to, and quality of, secondary education and the governance of the sector. The Activity will be pursued through four sub-activities that will invest in new education infrastructure, expand and improve teacher training, reduce gender disparities in educational outcomes, and enhance the Government's information management system and use of such system for decision-making in the national education sector.

title.narrative: IRAP road safety rating

description.narrative:
Level Outcome of In September 2022, the GoCI and MCC agreed to officially modify the Compact agreement, significantly reducing the scope of the investments on the Boulevard VGE. As a result, the iRAP assessment completed in early 2022 no longer reflects the investments that were completed by the Compact along the Boulevard VGE, which centered only on the Koumassi intersection.
Following the reporting of data for this indicator for the Boulevard de la Paix disaggregation and the Yopougon Expressway disaggregation, works were permanently halted along these two sections due to forced evictions undertaken by local authorities. As such, the values reported for these two disaggregations reflect the safety elements of the final detailed designs but do not translate into any safety improvements along these two road segments.

As such, the values reported for these two disaggregations reflect the safety elements of the final detailed designs but do not translate into any safety improvements along these two road segments. Actual

title.narrative: Students participating in MCC-supported education activities

description.narrative: Cumulative Outcome of The first cohort of students began training on March 25, 2021 with 21 students including 3 women. The second cohort started courses on January 6, 2022 with 20 students including 4 women. The third cohort began classes on September 1, 2022. There are 23 students in this third cohort including 8 women. The call for applications for the recruitment of a fourth cohort has been launched and submission deadline was September 31, 2024. Selection panels has been set up in Octobre - December 2024 to recruit and finalize the list of admitted candidates on January 10, 2025. The fourth cohort of students began training on February 6, 2025 with 17 students including 2 women. There is no more data expected for this indicator.

title.narrative: International Roughness Index of primary roads at end of construction contract

description.narrative:
Level Output of As reflected in the project work plans and Annex II of the M&E Plan, data on the International Roughness Index were expected to be reported during Year 5 of the Compact. However, the construction and rehabilitation works on the roads were significantly delayed and did not begin until early 2023. Works were subsequently halted along the Yopougon Expressway and Boulevard de la Paix due to forced evictions undertaken by local authorities, with no major rehabilitation works occuring along these segments. IRI data are thus not reported for these segments.
The IRI measurements were carried out on the Boulevard Port / Vridi on June 17, 2025 following the completion of works and found an average IRI of 4.9 (see ATP Q25 Anx5a M�sures IRI BPV 2025 page 16 ).
In September 2022, the GoCI and MCC agreed to officially modify the Compact agreement, significantly reducing the scope of the investments on the Boulevard VGE to the 0.7 kilometer flyover at the Koumassi intersection. Following this modification, the IRI was no longer a contractual obligation for the construction firm and could not be reported for Boulevard VGE at the end of the compact. However, the independent evaluator will collect and report this data as part of their work, which is expected to continue through 2028.

title.narrative: People trained in network prioritization

description.narrative:
Cumulative Output of
Ten training sessions took place from February 2020 to April 2021 and focused on: Module 1 � Traffic flow simulation; Module 2 � Design, monitoring and rehabilitation; Module 3 � Road network assessment; Module 4 � Construction and rehabilitation contracts; Module 5 � Planning and cost; Module 6 � Quality management tools; Module 7 � GIS; Module 8 � Environmental and Social Assessment of Infrastructure Projects; Module 9 � Urban Ecosystems; and Module 10 � Resettlement. A total of 116 people, including 27 women and 89 men, were trained and received a training certificate.

title.narrative: Percentage reduction in the amount of debt contracted by FER

description.narrative: Level Output of The negative number reported for this indicator corresponds to an increase in FER's debt. At the Compact Entry into Force, the amount of debt FER owed to banks and contractors (outstanding accounts payable past 120 days) was 125.716 billion FCFA (including 110.593 billion FCFA for bank debts and 15.123 billion FCFA for contractor debts payable past 120 days). As of December 31, 2024, the amount of FER's debt was 243.625 billion FCFA, comprised entirely of bank debt and with contractor debts payable past 120 days having been reduced to zero as agreed with MCC. This represents an increase in FER's debt of 93.79%.

title.narrative: Road asset inventory database created for the District of Abidjan

description.narrative: Date Output of As reflected in the project work plans and Annex II of the M&E Plan, the road asset inventory database for the District of Abidjan should have been completed and available for use on January 31, 2022 (Year 3 - Q11). On March 31, 2022, the development of the database was completed, including data for a representative sample of 1000 km of linear road network in the District of Abidjan. The system is operational and installed at AGEROUTE, which will ensure the database management.

title.narrative: Road safety database for the District of Abidjan created

description.narrative: Date Output of The Technical Assistance firm carried out several activities on the accidentology component of this work such as the geolocation of dangerous locations and intersections in Abidjan, the description of the main causes, recommendations for the design and improvement of the road safety policy, the accident data form and a data collection procedure adapted to Abidjan. However, the road safety database was not completed prior to the end of the compact.

title.narrative: Road Users Associations participation on the FER board of directors

description.narrative: Level Output of FER provided the data and source documents during Q21 but after the September 2024 QDRP process had already been completed. The signed attendance sheets and official meeting minutes of one FER board meetings during Compact Year 5 indicate that a Government official attended the respective FER board meetings in both their official capacity as a FER board member representing the Government and also acted as a proxy for a road user association's representative during this same meeting. Also, during three FER board meetings during Compact Year 5, a road user association's representative attended the respective FER board meetings in both their official capacity as a FER board member and also acted as a proxy for a Government official during those same meetings. There is nothing inherently problematic with having an individual serve as a proxy for a board member in instances where the board member is unavailable, and indeed there are specific statutes and decrees that provide for this. However, in light of the definition of this indicator � which measures the presence of road user associations � as well as the project logic result the indicator is designed to capture (i.e., �Improved road user oversight of FER�), it is not possible to count a Government official serving as proxy for a road user association when calculating the numerator for this indicator and vice versa. When calculating this indicator for Compact Year 6 in line with what is outlined above, out of the four meetings that were held during the year, two meetings (October 30, 2024 and August 5, 2025) do not meet the minimum threshold for the presence of road user associations. Thus, the final value reported for this indicator for Compact Year 6 is 50%.

description.narrative: Cumulative Process of As reflected in the project work plans and Annex II of the M&E plan, reporting on this indicator should have started in Year 2 of the Compact, which ended in August 2021 (Q9). However, due to delays linked to the COVID-19 pandemic and other factors, reporting on this indicator did not start until Q15. All the road construction and rehabilitation contracts were signed between MCA-C�te d'Ivoire and the contractors during calendar year 2023. The MCA financial system used the exchange rate on the day of payment and automatically calculated gains or losses due to the variation of the exchange rate. The average exchange rate calculated at the begining of each period is only used for the revaluation of contracts denominated in CFA francs (XOF) but not for payments.

title.narrative: Infrastructure Activity

description.narrative: Cote d'Ivoire - Transportation Project - Infrastructure Activity: This Activity will focus on the rehabilitation of up to 32 kilometers of critical roadway and adjoining infrastructure in the central corridor of Abidjan to improve overall travel times, improve traffic movement through improved geometric alignment and signalization, improve road safety, and integrate multi-modal planning (coordination with alternative, corresponding or nearby transport systems), to reduce household transport costs and increase revenue for businesses.

MCC Funding will be used to rehabilitate an approximate 9 km, six-lane section (three (3) lanes in each direction, plus two two-lane service-lanes) from Felix Houphou�t-Boigny Bridge to Akwaba Intersection

BMCC Funding will be used to rehabilitate an approximate combined 8 km, four-lane section (two lanes in each direction) that consist of (i) from the Felix Houphou�t-Boigny Bridge to the Tri Postal Intersection and the Vridi Industrial Zone, (ii) from the Tri Postal Intersection to Bus N� 19 Terminal of the Boulevard to Vridi, (iii) the adjoining Boulevard de Petit Bassam roundabout, and (iv) the existing 100 meter bridge along the Vridi Canal.
MCC Funding will be used to rehabilitate an approximate 7 km section of the six-lane Boulevard de la Paix.
MCC Funding will be used to rehabilitate an approximate 8 km section of the six-lane Yopougon Expressway from Adjame Bridge/�Pont Ferrailles� and ending at the Gesco intersection.

condition.narrative: Further details on conditions precedent affecting this activity can be found in the top-level parent activities.

Prior to Disbursement of Program Funding for Transport Investments on Boulevard du Port, Boulevard de Vridi, and Boulevard de Petit Bassam, the Government must have made available the necessary land with clean or proper title, in or near the Port, but away from the Transport Infrastructure Activity, where trucks will be required to relocate for short-term Port parking, prior to works in each such zone, as determined necessary by MCC.

Prior to the Disbursement for construction works under the Road Maintenance Fund Sub-Activity, the private sector or road user participation on the board of directors of FER will have increased to a minimum of 50 per cent.

Prior to the Disbursement of Program Funding for a particular works or construction contract for the Abidjan Transport Project, MCA-C�te d'Ivoire must develop and implement a site-specific traffic management plan and the provision of other protections during construction in order to establish effective and safe separation between road users and the construction works during all phases of works and construction, and maintain or enhance traffic flows, in form and substance satisfactory to MCC

usg:usg-activity.usg:purpose-statement: Cote d'Ivoire - Transportation Project - Infrastructure Activity: This Activity will focus on the rehabilitation of up to 32 kilometers of critical roadway and adjoining infrastructure in the central corridor of Abidjan to improve overall travel times, improve traffic movement through improved geometric alignment and signalization, improve road safety, and integrate multi-modal planning (coordination with alternative, corresponding or nearby transport systems), to reduce household transport costs and increase revenue for businesses.

title.narrative: Transportation Management and Planning Activity

description.narrative: Cote d'Ivoire - Transportation Project - Transportation Management and Planning Activity: The Activity will focus on building the technical and managerial capacity of the Government's road-transport related agencies through improved educational know-how and infrastructure asset-management techniques, which integrate the engineering, economics, environmental, and social elements and activities related to road design, preservation and maintenance. MCC Funding will support three inter-related sub-activities that (i) invest in educational and training resources for road asset management, (ii) develop road asset and safety resources and management tools, and (iii) improve the use of road maintenance funds. A fourth sub-activity will focus on helping the Government resolve the persistent problem of heavy-truck parking near and around the Port of Abidjan. The Compact will provide this support to and through Cote d'Ivoire's road-transport agencies.

usg:usg-activity.usg:purpose-statement: Cote d'Ivoire - Transportation Project - Transportation Management and Planning Activity: The Activity will focus on building the technical and managerial capacity of the Government's road-transport related agencies through improved educational know-how and infrastructure asset-management techniques, which integrate the engineering, economics, environmental, and social elements and activities related to road design, preservation and maintenance. MCC Funding will support three inter-related sub-activities that (i) invest in educational and training resources for road asset management, (ii) develop road asset and safety resources and management tools, and (iii) improve the use of road maintenance funds. A fourth sub-activity will focus on helping the Government resolve the persistent problem of heavy-truck parking near and around the Port of Abidjan. The Compact will provide this support to and through Cote d'Ivoire's road-transport agencies.
